lessons: Cut Think Twice and the second Night Terrors for a flier or removal spell; my UB deck ran both and went 1-2, though the guide's UB line says removal and evasion.

The guide's 'UB works with removal and evasion' was contradicted: my deck had Dead Weight, Claustrophobia, Sensory Deprivation, Tribute to Hunger and five fliers, yet lost 0-2 to BR at 21 and 20 turns.
Hold removal for fliers and big blockers as the guide says, and expect 23-to-29-turn stalls: my WG round went 1-2 with games of 29, 29 and 23 turns.
Pack 1's late picks went to Curiosity and Curse of the Bloody Tome, yet my only real answers were Fiend Hunter and Feeling of Dread; take removal over those.
Cutting Lost in the Mist, Mask of Avacyn and the 5-drops for a low curve won Round 2 in 16 turns but lost the 24-35 turn grinds to UB and UR; keep one late threat.
Round 3's UR evasive threats (Delver of Secrets, Stitched Drake, Invisible Stalker) beat me 0-2; spend late picks on cheap flying blockers, since Cellar Door and Mulch never made my deck.
Black-red worked as the guide predicted: Dead Weight, Victim of Night, Devil's Play and Morkrut Banshee answered threats while two Vampire Interlopers and Screeching Bat won, going 3-0 with 17 lands.
Tonight refines the guide's ground-body warning: my 3-0 BR deck was mostly ground creatures like Ashmouth Hound and Kessig Wolf, and it won because removal answered the fliers.
Burn removal flowed (Brimstone Volley, Geistflame, Harvest Pyre), but the 55-turn Round 1 loss showed my UR deck lacked late power, so take Stromkirk Noble over a fourth cheap spell.
Round 2's 0-2 loss to WU, which also ran Snapcaster Mage and Moon Heron, showed my blue fliers weren't winning races, so prioritize evasive threats over a third Riot Devils.
Cheap interaction like Blazing Torch and Grasp of Phantoms was in the deck that won 2-0 in Round 3, so keep taking it over marginal late creatures.
Pick one lane by mid pack 1: my pack 2 first pick, Brimstone Volley, went unused in a WG deck, exactly the off-colour removal trap the guide warns about.
The guide's ground cap is soft: WG with about ten ground creatures went 2-1, but the 35-turn round-2 loss was a stall that needed evasion, not more Thraben Sentry.
Tonight contradicted the guide: WG ran Spider Spawning and went 2-1, so 'Spider Spawning does not carry a ground deck' is not settled.
Take playable blue-red creatures early; Kruin Outlaw, Scourge of Geier Reach, Stitched Drake and Pitchburn Devils carried the 5-2 game record, while pick-4 Smite the Monstrous went unused.
Round 1's 1-2 loss to WG came in 16-24 turn grinds against Moment of Heroism and Slayer of the Wicked; prioritize evasive threats and cheap removal like Harvest Pyre over Dream Twist.
Cut the Curses, Furor and Vampiric Fury for 17 basics split 9 Island and 8 Mountain; the focused UR deck won 2-0 in two rounds.
My 2-1 BG deck had one true evasive finisher, Orchard Spirit, and won its long stalls anyway; aim for four evasive or removal-backed finishers before locking the build.
Seat 2's BR beat my BG deck 0-2 in 11-turn games, so the guide's 'block early against BR' held; keep cheap blockers like Ambush Viper in the 23.
Tonight contradicted the guide's skip of Darkthicket Wolf: my BG deck ran it and went 2-1 in matches, but only 4-4 in games, so it is marginal, not proven bad.
Prioritise a clock over a fourth 2/2 Walking Corpse: my WB games stalled at 22-28 turns, and the UR decks with Stitched Drake and Moon Heron were the ones that beat me.
Draft evasive finishers like Falkenrath Noble before filler: my 23rd card, Abbey Griffin, was the only added flyer, and my 1-6 game record came from a deck that could not close.
Take removal that also deals with fliers and big green threats, since Tribute to Hunger and Corpse Lunge did not stop the 25-turn Round 1 grind against Boneyard Wurm and Kindercatch.
